# Infolife
Infolife is that which lives in Netspace or on other electronic devices. This ranges from uploaded minds to artificial and emergent intelligences. Some notable examples are the cladists, uploaded minds living in the System (often called Lagrange); sprites, which are emergent intelligences; and memorial uploads, those who, at one point, had a neuroprint taken and who now live on in Netspace, even though they have died in the embodied world. However, even some of those who still life in Wetspace can be considered infolife, as much of their lives takes place in sims and virtual realities online, with only the token amount of energy paid to their needs offline.
There are several forms of uploaded consciousness going all the way back to the early and mid 22nd century. As such became more common, standards began to form, with the most common being the neuroprint — a means by which a snapshot of a consciousness is taken — and the NIRN (Neuro-Internal Resolution Network), a virtual brain in a jar which can run, among other things, a consciousness captured by a neuroprint.
## The System
Most pertinent, given the association with the System Consortium, are the cladists, those who have uploaded to the System, a computer which houses their consciousnesses and the first successful form of uploaded consciousnesses. This is a one-way, destructive process, meaning that the body does not survive after the mind is uploaded, but it is also a form of emigration, as the System is considered a separate legal entity from the rest of the nations of Earth. For many years, those sys-side were seen as isolationist, despite the means by which they encouraged others phys-side to upload. This was due to their focus on protecting the continuity of their lives, though it had the knock-on effect of being seen as escapist, unconcerned with the problems of the physical world such as the climate crisis.
Up until the 2500s, cladists had been restricted solely to life sys-side. There had been much resistance to ‘downloading’ leading up to this. It was seen as too risky, as it would allow another vector for those who so valued life as to upload to be taken advantage of, to fall into the machinations of capitalism and greed, as had so many other forms of life. Views on this, however, slowly began to loosen as did the grip of capitalism over the world phys-side. As humanity began to reach for the stars once more, cladists began to dream. Those sys-side wanted to participate in Earth’s second space age, too.
Starting in about 2535, committees began to congeal and working groups formed. One notable clade, the Odists (whose name was well known both sys- and phys-side from their various projects in the preceding centuries) being who they are, wormed their way into this process. One Odist in particular, May Then My Name Die With Me, was at the forefront of one such group focused on recovering corrupted core dumps via downloading. Once it became clear that this might actually be possible, she became one of the loudest proponents of the project and the pace leapt forward.
The first successful download happened in 2546, thanks to research overseen by both SysCon and the UN. Expensive as it is to produce biological bodies that can house positronic brains, downloads are still limited by 2550. Many downloads remained on Earth, but many more joined the crews of various stations.
Downloaded cladists can reconcile with their counterparts sys-side (providing they have an instance remaining there), essentially re-uploading and merging with their down-trees, though this has led to some strife as they learn more about life phys-side. Life tethered to the physical world is tough for some, especially the older uploads who have only known uploaded life for centuries.
